sealed.statement: A durable cluster identity is minted exactly once at first seed bootstrap as a replicated CONFIG-row singleton, carried node-locally in the rejoin hints (both builders) with a fail-closed typed CLUSTER_ID_MISMATCH auto-rejoin decision when the hints identity mismatches the expected one, and threaded into the raft snapshot-checkpoint identity seam (replacing the config-pinned 'lagrange-default-cluster' default while the row is visible). doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/cluster-identity-persistence-seam.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — mint, hints-carriage, CONFIG-row persistence, seam wiring, and fail-closed mismatch receipts all passing.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Persist cluster identity through the existing raft snapshot-checkpoint clusterId seam (src/raft/snapshot-catchup-constants.js), whose own comment records that no durable cluster identity exists; do not invent a parallel identity concept.

The bootstrap request must carry expectedClusterId and the seed must reject mismatches with a typed refusal classified as terminal; a missing expectedClusterId from a pre-identity joiner is handled by explicit compatibility policy, not silent acceptance.

A cluster-id mismatch at any durable evidence source (rejoin hints, authoritative row, snapshot checkpoint) must fail closed with a typed identity-mismatch outcome, never fall through to fresh seed or join.
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding mint/persist/reject mechanism is reverted while the rest of the change remains.

The oracle evidence files must be written by a deterministic evidence harness that re-runs the recorded proof commands (focused test files, red-on-revert checks, seam wiring audits) at quest terminal; no hand-authored metric values.
